title: Endocrine and metabolic emergencies
summary: Recognise and treat the endocrine emergencies seen in Indian ICUs: DKA (including euglycaemic DKA with SGLT2 inhibitors), HHS, adrenal crisis, thyroid storm and myxoedema coma, plus ICU glucose targets and hypoglycaemia.

topics.title: Diabetic ketoacidosis (including euglycaemic DKA)
topics.summary: DKA = diabetes or glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL + β-hydroxybutyrate ≥ 3.0 mmol/L (or urine ketones ≥ 2+) + pH < 7.3 and/or HCO3- < 18. Treat with fluids, fixed-rate insulin 0.1 units/kg/h once K+ ≥ 3.5, potassium replacement, and dextrose once glucose < 250 mg/dL until ketones clear.

definition.text: ADA/EASD/JBDS 2024: D (glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL or known diabetes), K (β-hydroxybutyrate ≥ 3.0 mmol/L or urine ketones ≥ 2+), A (pH < 7.3 and/or bicarbonate < 18 mmol/L).

steps.title: Fluids
steps.detail: 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid 500-1000 mL/h for the first 2-4 h (250 mL boluses if elderly, heart or kidney failure). Balanced fluids resolve DKA faster with less hyperchloraemia.

steps.title: Potassium first
steps.detail: K+ < 3.5: give KCl 10 mmol/h and delay insulin until > 3.5. K+ 3.5-5.0: add 20-30 mmol KCl per litre to keep 4-5. K+ > 5.0: no K+, recheck in 2 h.

steps.title: Insulin
steps.detail: Fixed-rate IV regular insulin 0.1 units/kg/h (0.1 units/kg bolus if access delayed). Continue the patient's basal insulin; or start basal 0.15-0.3 units/kg SC early.

steps.title: Glucose < 250 mg/dL
steps.detail: Add 5-10% dextrose and reduce insulin to 0.05 units/kg/h; keep glucose ~200 mg/dL; never stop insulin while ketotic. Euglycaemic DKA: start dextrose with the saline from the outset.

steps.title: Every 1-2 h / 4 h
steps.detail: Capillary glucose hourly; K+ at 2 h then 4-hourly; electrolytes, β-hydroxybutyrate, venous pH every 4 h.

steps.title: Only pH < 7.0
steps.detail: 100 mmol 8.4% in 400 mL water over 2 h, repeat until pH > 7.0. Phosphate only if < 1.0 mg/dL with weakness.

steps.title: Then transition
steps.detail: Ketones < 0.6 mmol/L and venous pH ≥ 7.3 or HCO3- ≥ 18. Give SC basal-bolus insulin (0.5-0.6 units/kg/day; 0.3 if frail/CKD), overlap 1-2 h before stopping IV insulin.

doseCards.dose: 0.1 units/kg/h; reduce to 0.05 units/kg/h when glucose < 250 mg/dL with dextrose added
doseCards.workedExample: 60 kg: 6 units/h (6 mL/h of 1 unit/mL) → 3 units/h with 10% dextrose once glucose < 250
doseCards.verify: Prepare by units (U-40 vs U-100 vials).

doseCards.dose: 100 mmol (100 mL 8.4%) in 400 mL sterile water over 2 h, repeat to pH > 7.0

tables.title: DKA severity (ADA 2024)
tables.caption: Not all variables need to be met; level of care is a clinical decision. Mild-moderate DKA can be treated with hourly-2-hourly SC rapid-acting analogues.

redFlags.text: K+ < 3.5 on arrival: insulin waits until potassium is replaced.
Falling GCS during treatment, especially in young patients: cerebral oedema; mannitol and CT.
Euglycaemic DKA on SGLT2 inhibitors (glucose < 200 mg/dL): missed if only glucose is checked.

pitfalls.text: Stopping insulin when glucose normalises while ketones persist.
Using anion gap or urine ketones to define resolution (hyperchloraemia and acetoacetate conversion mislead).
Stopping IV insulin without overlapping SC basal insulin → rebound DKA.

pearls.text: Bedside β-hydroxybutyrate meters make monitoring easy and cheap; urine ketones are a poor substitute.
Look for the trigger: infection, missed insulin, MI, pancreatitis, SGLT2 inhibitor.

nodes.text: KCl 10 mmol/h; hold insulin until K+ > 3.5
Insulin 0.1 units/kg/h; KCl 20-30 mmol/L if K+ 3.5-5.0
SC basal-bolus; stop IV after 1-2 h overlap

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: - Insulin deficiency plus counter-regulatory hormones drive lipolysis and ketogenesis; osmotic diuresis causes total-body K+ deficit of 3-6 mmol/kg even if serum K+ is high.
consultantNotes.evidence: - **ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS 2024 consensus:** new glucose threshold (≥ 200 mg/dL or known diabetes), β-hydroxybutyrate-based diagnosis and resolution, balanced crystalloids acceptable.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Early SC basal insulin during IV infusion shortens time to resolution in small studies without more hypoglycaemia.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Reported inpatient DKA mortality in India has been as high as 30% in some series, mostly due to late presentation and infection. Ketosis-prone type 2 diabetes is common.

options: Ketones < 0.6 mmol/L and pH ≥ 7.3 or HCO3- ≥ 18
quiz.explanation: Anion gap and urine ketones mislead.

quiz.stem: On empagliflozin, glucose 170 mg/dL, BHB 5.2, pH 7.12:
options: Euglycaemic DKA: dextrose + insulin from the start

topics.title: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (HHS)
topics.summary: HHS = glucose ≥ 600 mg/dL, effective osmolality > 300 mOsm/kg, minimal ketosis and no significant acidosis. Rehydrate first and slowly; fall in osmolality 3-8 mOsm/kg/h and in Na+ ≤ 10 mmol/L/24 h; low-dose insulin 0.05 units/kg/h once glucose stops falling with fluid alone.

definition.text: Glucose ≥ 600 mg/dL; calculated effective osmolality > 300 mOsm/kg (or total > 320); β-hydroxybutyrate < 3.0 mmol/L (urine ketones < 2+); pH ≥ 7.3 and HCO3- ≥ 15 mmol/L.

steps.title: Fluids
steps.detail: 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid 500-1000 mL/h for 2-4 h; deficit is ~100-220 mL/kg; correct over 24-48 h.

steps.title: Sodium may rise
steps.detail: A rising Na+ as glucose falls is expected (1.6 mmol/L per 100 mg/dL); switch to 0.45% saline only if osmolality is not falling despite positive balance.

steps.title: Low dose, later
steps.detail: 0.05 units/kg/h when glucose stops falling with fluids alone (or immediately if mixed DKA/HHS with BHB ≥ 3: 0.1 units/kg/h). Glucose fall ≤ 90-120 mg/dL/h.

steps.title: Rates
steps.detail: Osmolality fall 3-8 mOsm/kg/h; Na+ fall ≤ 10 mmol/L/24 h; keep glucose 200-300 mg/dL in the first 24 h.

steps.title: Complications
steps.detail: Prophylactic LMWH (prothrombotic state), pressure care, look for infection, MI, stroke. Resolution: osmolality < 300, UO > 0.5 mL/kg/h, cognition improved, glucose < 250.

doseCards.dose: 0.05 units/kg/h, started when glucose no longer falls with fluids

redFlags.text: Seizures or worsening GCS during treatment: too-rapid osmolality fall; cerebral oedema or osmotic demyelination.

pitfalls.text: Treating HHS like DKA with high-dose insulin early, causing rapid osmotic shifts and circulatory collapse.
Starting hypotonic fluids because Na+ rises early.

pearls.text: Calculate effective osmolality every 1-2 h at the start; plot glucose, Na+ and osmolality on a chart.

nodes.text: 0.45% saline if osmolality not falling despite positive balance
Continue; LMWH; treat trigger until resolved

consultantNotes.evidence: - **ADA 2024 consensus**, drawing on JBDS HHS guidance: delayed low-dose insulin and slow osmolar correction.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Elderly people with untreated type 2 diabetes, infections (UTI, pneumonia) and summer dehydration are the classic Indian presentation; mortality is 5-10× that of DKA.

options: 0.05 units/kg/h once glucose stops falling with fluids

quiz.stem: Na+ rises from 140 to 146 as glucose falls 400 mg/dL. Action:
options: Expected; continue isotonic fluid if osmolality falling
quiz.explanation: Corrected Na+ rises as glucose drops.

topics.title: Adrenal crisis
topics.summary: Unexplained shock, vomiting, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia or hypoglycaemia in someone at risk (steroid use, Addison's, pituitary disease): give hydrocortisone 100 mg IV immediately after a random cortisol, without waiting for results, plus 1 L isotonic fluid in the first hour.

steps.title: Who
steps.detail: Long-term or recently stopped glucocorticoids (including inhaled/topical high dose), known Addison's or hypopituitarism, post-partum haemorrhage (Sheehan's), adrenal haemorrhage on anticoagulants or in meningococcaemia, TB or HIV adrenalitis, checkpoint inhibitors, etomidate.

steps.title: Treat now
steps.detail: Draw random cortisol (+ ACTH if possible), then hydrocortisone 100 mg IV/IM bolus. Do not wait for results or a stimulation test.

steps.title: Fluids
steps.detail: 1 L 0.9% saline (or 5% dextrose in saline if hypoglycaemic) within the first hour, then guided by haemodynamics.

steps.title: Continue
steps.detail: Hydrocortisone 200 mg/24 h as continuous infusion or 50 mg IV every 6 h; taper to oral maintenance over 1-3 days once the trigger is controlled.

steps.title: Prevent
steps.detail: Sick-day rules (double oral dose during febrile illness), steroid card, IM hydrocortisone emergency kit; treat the trigger (infection, surgery, missed doses).

doseCards.dose: 100 mg bolus, then 200 mg/24 h infusion or 50 mg 6-hourly
doseCards.notes: Children: 50 mg/m² (approx. 2 mg/kg, max 100 mg) bolus.

redFlags.text: Refractory hypotension in a patient on long-term steroids: give hydrocortisone even before a cortisol level returns.

pitfalls.text: Giving dexamethasone instead (no mineralocorticoid effect) unless doing a stimulation test.
Starting thyroxine before steroids in combined hypopituitarism (can precipitate crisis).

pearls.text: Hyperkalaemia suggests primary (adrenal) failure; secondary (pituitary) failure usually has normal K+.

nodes.text: 1 L 0.9% saline over 1 h; check glucose
Hydrocortisone 200 mg/24 h; treat trigger; taper over 1-3 days
Continue steroid; look for other shock causes

consultantNotes.evidence: - **Endocrine Society 2016:** immediate parenteral hydrocortisone 100 mg, then 200 mg/24 h; fluid resuscitation with isotonic saline.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Over-the-counter steroid use (including adulterated ayurvedic/herbal preparations) and tuberculous adrenalitis are important Indian causes; Sheehan's syndrome still occurs.

topics.title: Thyroid storm and myxoedema coma
topics.summary: Thyroid storm: Burch-Wartofsky score ≥ 45 → β-blocker, thionamide (PTU preferred), iodine ≥ 1 h later, hydrocortisone, cooling and treatment of the trigger. Myxoedema coma: supportive care, hydrocortisone first, then thyroxine.

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.detail: Fever, tachycardia/AF, heart failure, agitation/delirium, GI/hepatic dysfunction with thyrotoxicosis. Burch-Wartofsky ≥ 45 highly suggestive; 25-44 impending storm.

steps.title: β-block
steps.detail: Propranolol 60-80 mg every 4 h (also reduces T4→T3); esmolol infusion if haemodynamically fragile.

steps.title: Block synthesis
steps.detail: PTU 500-1000 mg load then 250 mg every 4 h (or methimazole 60-80 mg/day).

steps.title: Block release
steps.detail: Iodine at least 1 h after the thionamide: SSKI 5 drops (0.25 mL) every 6 h or Lugol's iodine.

steps.title: Steroid + support
steps.detail: Hydrocortisone 300 mg IV load then 100 mg every 8 h; paracetamol and active cooling (avoid aspirin); fluids; treat infection. Plasmapheresis or urgent thyroidectomy if refractory.

steps.title: Recognise
steps.detail: Hypothermia, coma, bradycardia, hypoventilation (hypercapnia), hyponatraemia, hypoglycaemia in long-standing hypothyroidism, often triggered by infection, cold, sedatives.

steps.title: Treat
steps.detail: Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV 8-hourly until adrenal insufficiency excluded, then levothyroxine IV 200-400 mcg load and 1.6 mcg/kg/day × 0.75 IV (lower doses in elderly/cardiac); ventilate for hypercapnia; passive rewarming.

doseCards.dose: 500-1000 mg load, then 250 mg every 4 h
300 mg load, then 100 mg every 8 h
200-400 mcg load, then 1.6 mcg/kg/day × 0.75 IV daily
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg, no cardiac disease: 300 mcg IV, then ~85 mcg IV daily
doseCards.verify: NG regimens (e.g. 300-500 mcg load) are used in India where IV is unavailable; confirm with local endocrinology.

tables.title: Burch-Wartofsky point scale (summary)
rows: CNS: mild agitation / delirium, psychosis, lethargy / seizure or coma
GI-hepatic: diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain / unexplained jaundice
Heart failure: mild (oedema) / moderate (bibasal crackles) / severe (pulmonary oedema)
tables.caption: Score ≥ 45 highly suggestive of storm; 25-44 impending; < 25 unlikely.

redFlags.text: Thyroid storm with low-output heart failure: β-blockers can precipitate collapse; use esmolol with echo guidance.

pitfalls.text: Giving iodine before the thionamide (fuels hormone synthesis).
Full-dose thyroxine without steroid cover in myxoedema coma.

pearls.text: Free T4/T3 levels do not separate storm from uncomplicated thyrotoxicosis; the diagnosis is clinical.

nodes.text: PTU 500-1000 mg load then 250 mg q4h
Hydrocortisone 300 mg then 100 mg q8h; cool

consultantNotes.evidence: - **ATA 2016 (hyperthyroidism)** and **ATA 2014 (hypothyroidism)** guidelines; Burch & Wartofsky 1993 scoring system.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Untreated Graves' disease and post-partum presentations are common. Lugol's iodine is cheap and available; IV levothyroxine is not widely stocked.

topics.title: Glucose control in the ICU
topics.summary: Start an insulin protocol when glucose is persistently ≥ 180 mg/dL, titrate to 140-200 mg/dL (not 80-139), monitor at least hourly while unstable, and treat hypoglycaemia immediately.

steps.title: ≥ 180 mg/dL twice
steps.detail: Two consecutive values ≥ 180 mg/dL (10 mmol/L): review glucose sources (dextrose, feeds, steroids) and start an IV insulin protocol.

steps.title: 140-200 mg/dL
steps.detail: SCCM 2024 suggests against an 80-139 mg/dL target because of hypoglycaemia. NICE-SUGAR (81-108 mg/dL) increased 90-day mortality (27.5% vs 24.9%).

steps.title: IV infusion
steps.detail: Continuous IV insulin with an explicit decision-support protocol rather than SC sliding scales in unstable patients.

steps.title: ≤ 1 hourly
steps.detail: Hourly checks during instability; arterial or venous samples on a blood-gas analyser are more accurate than capillary meters in shock or oedema.

steps.title: When stable and eating
steps.detail: Basal-bolus SC insulin, ~60-80% of the stable 24-h IV requirement, basal overlapping 1-2 h before stopping infusion.

redFlags.text: Glucose < 70 mg/dL on insulin: stop insulin, give dextrose, find the cause (feed interrupted, renal failure, sepsis, liver failure).

pitfalls.text: Insulin continues at full rate when enteral feeds are stopped for procedures.
Capillary meter readings in shocked, oedematous patients.

pearls.text: TGC-fast (no early PN): tight control 80-110 mg/dL did not change ICU length of stay or mortality.

nodes.text: Stop insulin; 15-25 g IV dextrose; recheck 15 min
Continue; transition to SC when stable

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **NICE-SUGAR 2009 (n = 6104):** intensive 81-108 mg/dL increased mortality and severe hypoglycaemia.
- **TGC-fast 2023 (n = 9230):** tight control without early parenteral nutrition: no difference in ICU dependency or mortality.
- **SCCM 2024:** suggest against 80-139 mg/dL; target 140-200 mg/dL.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Individualised targets based on HbA1c (higher targets in chronic poor control) are promising but unproven.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Nursing workload and cost of strips limit hourly checks; a written nurse-driven protocol with blood-gas glucose is a practical compromise.

topics.title: Hypoglycaemia
topics.summary: Glucose < 70 mg/dL (level 1), < 54 mg/dL (level 2) or any value with cognitive impairment needing help (level 3). Give 15-25 g IV dextrose or IM glucagon, recheck at 15 min, then find and treat the cause; sulphonylurea overdose needs prolonged dextrose ± octreotide.

definition.text: Level 1 < 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L); level 2 < 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L); level 3 severe event with altered mental or physical state requiring assistance.

steps.title: Treat
steps.detail: Conscious and able to swallow: 15-20 g oral glucose. Otherwise IV: 15-25 g dextrose (150-200 mL 10% or 50 mL 50% via a large vein). No IV: glucagon 1 mg IM/SC.

steps.title: Recheck
steps.detail: Repeat treatment until > 70 mg/dL, then give a long-acting carbohydrate or start a 10% dextrose infusion.

steps.title: Find it
steps.detail: Insulin (including stopped feeds), sulphonylureas, sepsis, liver failure, AKI/CKD, adrenal insufficiency, alcohol, malaria and quinine, insulinoma, salicylates.

steps.title: Prolonged risk
steps.detail: Admit for ≥ 24 h; continuous 10% dextrose; octreotide 50-100 mcg SC every 6-8 h for recurrent hypoglycaemia.

steps.title: If malnourished
steps.detail: Thiamine 100 mg IV with or before dextrose in alcohol use or malnutrition (do not delay glucose).

doseCards.workedExample: Glucose 38 mg/dL, GCS 9: 50 mL 50% dextrose via antecubital vein, recheck 15 min → 112 mg/dL; start 10% dextrose 50 mL/h

redFlags.text: Recurrent hypoglycaemia after an oral hypoglycaemic overdose: needs 24-72 h of monitoring.
Hypoglycaemia in septic shock or malaria: marker of severity.

pitfalls.text: Glucagon in liver failure, starvation or alcohol (no glycogen stores).

pearls.text: Always check glucose in anyone with altered sensorium, seizures or focal deficits.

consultantNotes.evidence: - **ADA Standards 2025 (hospital care):** classification, protocols for prevention and treatment.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Sulphonylurea use (glimepiride, gliclazide) is widespread; accidental or intentional overdose and elderly patients with CKD are common causes. Severe malaria and quinine cause hypoglycaemia.

drugs.name: Regular (soluble) insulin infusion
drugs.adultDose: DKA: fixed rate 0.1 units/kg/h (optional 0.1 units/kg bolus). HHS: 0.05 units/kg/h once glucose stops falling with fluids alone. ICU hyperglycaemia: protocol-driven to 140-180 mg/dL.
drugs.preparationIndia: 50 units in 50 mL 0.9% saline (1 unit/mL). Check vial strength: U-40 (40 units/mL) or U-100.
drugs.cautions: Hypokalaemia (do not start if K+ < 3.5 mmol/L), hypoglycaemia, hypophosphataemia.

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone
drugs.class: Glucocorticoid (with mineralocorticoid activity at high dose)
drugs.indications: Adrenal crisis; thyroid storm; myxoedema coma (until adrenal insufficiency excluded); septic shock.
drugs.adultDose: Adrenal crisis: 100 mg IV bolus, then 200 mg/24 h (continuous or 50 mg every 6 h); taper over 1-3 days once stable. Thyroid storm: 300 mg IV load then 100 mg every 8 h.
drugs.cautions: Hyperglycaemia, hypernatraemia; fludrocortisone not needed while hydrocortisone > 50 mg/day.

drugs.name: Propylthiouracil (PTU)
drugs.indications: Thyroid storm (preferred: also blocks T4→T3 conversion); first-trimester pregnancy.
drugs.adultDose: 500-1000 mg loading dose orally/NG, then 250 mg every 4 h.
drugs.cautions: Hepatotoxicity, agranulocytosis. Methimazole 60-80 mg/day is the alternative.

drugs.name: Propranolol
drugs.adultDose: 60-80 mg orally/NG every 4 h; IV 1 mg slowly, repeat. Esmolol infusion if unstable or asthma.
drugs.cautions: Thyrotoxic cardiomyopathy with low output: use esmolol cautiously with echo guidance.

drugs.name: Levothyroxine
drugs.adultDose: IV 200-400 mcg load, then 1.6 mcg/kg/day (IV dose ≈ 75% of oral); lower doses in elderly/cardiac disease.
drugs.preparationIndia: Tablets (NG) widely available; IV vials limited.
drugs.cautions: Precipitates myocardial ischaemia and arrhythmias; give hydrocortisone first.
drugs.verify: Confirm NG dosing regimen used locally when IV is unavailable.

drugs.name: Dextrose (glucose)
drugs.indications: Hypoglycaemia; with insulin in DKA once glucose < 250 mg/dL; hyperkalaemia.
drugs.adultDose: Hypoglycaemia: 15-25 g IV (e.g. 150-200 mL 10% or 50 mL 25% dextrose / 50 mL 50% via large vein), recheck at 15 min.
drugs.cautions: 50% is sclerosant: use a large vein and flush.

drugs.name: Potassium chloride
drugs.adultDose: K+ < 3.5: 10 mmol/h IV before insulin. K+ 3.5-5.0: 20-30 mmol per litre of IV fluid to keep K+ 4-5 mmol/L.
drugs.preparationIndia: 15% KCl 10 mL ampoule = 20 mmol; premixed bags preferred.
drugs.cautions: Never as an undiluted bolus; reduce in oliguria.

drugs.name: Sodium bicarbonate
drugs.adultDose: 100 mmol (100 mL 8.4%) in 400 mL sterile water over 2 h; repeat until pH > 7.0.
drugs.cautions: Hypokalaemia, paradoxical CSF acidosis, cerebral oedema risk in children.
